headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines while shorts liquidate and whales move coins cold, but funding turns mixed and the bounce shows wear at distance.
paragraphs: Regime is intact but fraying at the edges. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, and three of the seven majors (ETH, SOL, and XRP) have posted golden crosses, the signal of a 50-day line crossing above the 200-day. Yet the tape shows persistent compression: over the last month Bitcoin is up 16.2%, Ethereum up 23.9%, and Solana up 27.3%, but all three are down on the week and all are down on the day. The market cap fell 2.57% in 24 hours to 2.6 trillion dollars while Bitcoin dominance held at 59.1%. The regime is not broken, but the rebound is paying rent to the short end of the curve, not generating fresh conviction at scale.

Momentum and trend are diverging quietly. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 65.1, overbought territory, while its MACD has rolled over below its signal line. Ethereum and XRP show the same pattern: RSI in the 58-63 range but MACD below signal. Only Solana is still printing MACD above signal, though its RSI is 62.1 and the price is down 0.5% on the day despite a 4.2% weekly gain. This is the signature of a move that has run without fresh momentum behind it. When an asset climbs 27% in a month (Solana's case) on a flat-to-negative MACD, the climb is bought, not powered.

Positioning tells the tale of unequal conviction. Bitcoin and Ethereum are crowded longs: BTC's long-to-short ratio on perpetuals is 1.29 and ETH's is 1.63, while funding rates for both run positive and above 5% annualized (BTC at 5.1%, ETH at 6.4%). Traders are paying to hold those bets. Yet the liquidation window over the last 3 to 5 hours shows shorts being wiped out in size: ETH saw 1.3 million dollars of long liquidations against only 204,000 dollars of short liquidations, and Bitcoin saw 707,000 dollars of short liquidations against 160,000 of long liquidations. The crowded long positions are vindicated by the tape, but vindication in a downtrend is often the last act before the reversal. Solana is the outlier: its funding rate is negative at minus 5.1% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs to hold, and its long-to-short ratio is 1.95, still imbalanced but less extreme than the tier-1 names. XRP and Doge are even more lopsided, with ratios of 2.55 and 4.17 respectively, and both run hot funding (11% and 10.1% annualized), the posture of crowded, expensive leverage.

Flows paint a picture of retreat and reallocation. On September 1st, Bitcoin ETFs saw an outflow of 236.5 million dollars, but the last five sessions netted 252.8 million dollars inbound, so the single-day print is noise atop a constructive structure. Ethereum ETF flows are more consistent: inflows on the day (8.6 million dollars) and 616.5 million dollars over five sessions, with ten straight sessions in the same direction. In crypto's ecosystem itself, whale activity over the last 24 hours was flat at zero net moving off exchanges, a pause. But weekly data shows a reversal: the week ending August 26th saw 1.5 billion dollars move onto exchanges; the week ending September 2nd shows 344 million dollars moving off exchanges into cold storage. Stablecoin float rose 1.16% over 30 days to 309 billion dollars, a reserve buildup that has not yet activated into buying pressure. The buying power sits idle; coins are moving to cold storage. This tension, whales holding, exchanges lightening, stablecoins stockpiling, is a setup, not a confirmation.

Sentiment reads a steady 63 on the Fear and Greed index ("Greed" label) within a 30-day range of 25 to 74, so today is neither euphoric nor desperate. The crowd is calm and tilted to the upside, which matches the price structure above the 200-day lines but contradicts the momentum rollover and the positioning crowding. Doge and XRP, the most asymmetrically leveraged names, are the farthest from their 12-month highs: Doge is down 71.9% and XRP down 56.9%. Both are also down double digits on the week (Doge minus 12.8%, XRP minus 11.6%), yet both show positive funding rates, meaning traders are still paying to hold long exposure to the worst performers. This is the inverse of smart positioning: the crowd buys what has fallen the most and pays premium to do so, exactly the trade that precedes the shakeout.

Watch for three conditions to signal a shift. First, a reclaim of the 200-day moving average by any of the majors, with a close below it that persists through the next session. Second, a flip in ETH or BTC funding rates from positive to negative, which would signal longs are paying shorts instead of the reverse. Third, a reversal in weekly whale flows back onto exchanges after this week's 344 million dollar outflow, which would mean the cold storage bid is giving way to profit-taking. The tape is stretched between duration above trend and momentum rolling, and that is the condition to monitor.
